Recent work favors atomic claim evaluation over fluent explanations or text similarity. *On the Factual Consistency of Text-based Explainable Recommendation Models* (2025, revised 2026) measures statement-level factual consistency and relevance, finding that high semantic similarity can coexist with poor factual precision. Its review-derived evidence is unavailable here; transfer the claim-audit principle, not its data or pretrained evaluators. Metadata support also does not establish why SASRec ranked an item: *Walk the Talk?* (ICLR 2025) evaluates explanation faithfulness through counterfactual changes to purportedly influential concepts. [Factual consistency](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24366); [faithfulness](https://openreview.net/forum?id=4ub9gpx9xw).

Abstention should depend on evidence sufficiency, not broad topical relevance. *Sufficient Context* (ICLR 2025) distinguishes context containing enough information to answer from merely useful context. *Knowing When Not to Answer* (2026 preprint) decomposes claims into conditions and evaluates support/refutation/abstention using risk–coverage tradeoffs. These support an adapted evidence-coding approach, but do not validate a recommendation-specific taxonomy. [Sufficient Context](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/33dffa2e3d2ab74a783d1a8c292f66d9-Paper-Conference.pdf); [abstention-aware verification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14189).

Proposed application: audit full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the required twenty users, five/category. Record candidate/history IDs, timestamps, exact title/description spans, claim type, and supported/contradicted/unknown status. Distinguish duplicate-content evidence, possible substitutes, explicit compatibility conflicts, explicit complementary functions, and weak topical associations. Substitution alone does not establish unwanted redundancy; missing requirements or intent means unknown. Use available simulator feedback to identify coding disagreements, retaining its provenance rather than treating it as observed preference. Report evidence coverage and audited coding errors separately from macro validation HR@10; abstain on unsupported explanations without changing benchmark ranking evaluation.
